subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — SLA windowing, credit caps and response tiers
messages:
From: Sara Brooks <sara.brooks@atlashealth.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Thu, 4 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLA questions on Order Form v3

Hi Olga / Markus,

Thanks for sending v3 of the Order Form. Procurement and engineering had a quick pass and a few outstanding items on the SLA we need to resolve before legal will countersign:

- Can you confirm the maintenance blackout policy — specifically any single-day monthly blackout vs. a rolling 4-hour weekly window? Our launch calendar is tight and we need guaranteed blackout notice windows.
- The service credit cap is currently 100% of monthly fees. Can Redwood consider a capped basket (e.g., 50% monthly cap) for initial term?
- Response tiers: we need P1 response within 30 minutes (not 60). For healthcare workloads this is a must.

Attached are our annotated redlines for reference. Happy to jump on a call tomorrow if that helps.

Thanks,
Sara Brooks
Head of Platform Ops — AtlasHealth

Attachments: atlas_redlines_20251203.pdf
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: Sara Brooks <sara.brooks@atlashealth.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Dec 2025 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA questions on Order Form v3

Sara — thanks for the detailed pass and the annotated file. High-level responses inline:

- Maintenance windows: Redwood's standard is one 4-hour weekly maintenance window (scheduled at least 72 hours in advance) OR, by exception, a monthly 24-hour blackout slot for major upgrades. We can surface an explicit calendar windowing commitment in the order form rather than the generic language.
- Credit cap: We can agree to a 50% monthly cap for the initial 12-month term and reevaluate on renewal. We'll need procurement to accept that in the order form.
- P1 response: Our committed P1 acknowledgement is 30 minutes for Dedicated customers with the Enterprise support add-on; for Hosted customers it's 60. Given AtlasHealth's needs, we can include Enterprise support (already in the commercial term) which guarantees 30-minute acknowledgement and a 4-hour mitigation plan.

I'll loop Lauren from Legal to confirm the exact redline language for the maintenance carveouts and the credit cap. If acceptable, we can redline the order form and send to procurement for countersign.

Would a 30 minute slot tomorrow at 10am PT for a short sync work for you?

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20251204_redline_sla_summary.pdf
From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, Sara Brooks <sara.brooks@atlashealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Dec 2025 11:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA questions on Order Form v3

Looping in legal language proposals. Quick notes:

- Proposed maintenance clause: "Maintenance: Customer will be provided with at least 72 hours' notice for routine maintenance expected to impact service availability. Redwood may schedule up to one (1) four-hour maintenance window per calendar week; for a major release Redwood may schedule a single 24-hour maintenance window per calendar month with 7 days' notice. Scheduled maintenance will not be considered an outage for purposes of SLA credits."

- Credit cap clause (redline): "Service Credit Cap: The cumulative aggregate Service Credits paid to Customer in any billing month shall not exceed fifty percent (50%) of the Fees for such month for the first twelve (12) months of the Term. Thereafter, the Parties will revisit the cap during renewal negotiations."

- P1 response tier: change to 30-minute acknowledgement and 4-hour remediation plan for Dedicated + Enterprise support. For Hosted without Enterprise support maintain 60-minute acknowledgement.

I attached word redlines for insertion into the Order Form. If Atlas needs a lower remediation SLA (e.g., 2-hour fix), we need to discuss pricing/penalties.

-Markus

Attachments: orderform_v3_redlines.docx
From: Sara Brooks <sara.brooks@atlashealth.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com, Eliot Chen <eliot.chen@atlashealth.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Dec 2025 08:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA questions on Order Form v3

Thanks — the maintenance language looks better. A couple of follow-ups from Procurement:

1) Procurement still wants the credit cap to be a shared-risk model: 50% monthly cap but no cap on cumulative credits over a rolling 12-month period if repeated outages occur. Can Redwood accept an exception where repeated similar outages void the monthly cap?
2) For our BAU P1s we really need an internal RTO target (time to mitigation) rather than just acknowledgement. If you can commit to a 4-hour mitigation plan, can you also include an RTO target for critical call-paths (e.g., 6 hours to restore partial service for read-only APIs)?

We can do the 10am PT sync tomorrow — will bring our lead SRE.

-Sara
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: Sara Brooks <sara.brooks@atlashealth.com>, markus.klein@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 6 Dec 2025 14:52:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA questions on Order Form v3

Sara,

Appreciate the clear asks. Our proposed legal position to cover Atlas' procurement points:

- Repeated outage carveout: We are open to an exception where materially identical outages attributable to Redwood that occur more than three (3) times within any rolling 12-month period will be excluded from the monthly cap and subject to an escalated remediation and review plan. The definition of "materially identical outage" will be: outages caused by the same root cause as determined by joint post-incident analysis.

- RTO targets: We can add an RTO target for critical APIs for Dedicated deployments: restore partial read-only capability within six (6) hours and full service within twenty-four (24) hours, conditional on Atlas providing requested data and access for diagnostics. For Hosted we will include best-effort language and a commitment to prioritize critical call-paths.

I'll incorporate the proposed phrasing into the Order Form redlines and upload to the shared Drive. If you confirm the carveout wording I'll prepare a short addendum the procurement team can sign off on.

Best regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
